page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-48 is a compute-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor with x86_64 architecture. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 96 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It contains no local storage and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in compute-heavy tasks. The server achieved a Passmark CPU score of 54727.59 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 17695.0, both placing in the strong category. It demonstrates top-tier capabilities in image processing and small-model LLM text generation. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 277.22 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput was measured at 74.36 GB/sec. However, memory-bound operations are more moderate, with uncached large-block memory write bandwidth limited to 64.01 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highcpu-48 offers high compute density per resource unit, making it highly efficient for CPU-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints. The primary tradeoff is the low RAM-to-vCPU ratio and the complete lack of local storage, which requires external storage solutions. This profile is optimal for workloads such as software compilation, ray tracing, text and image processing, static web serving, and moderate LLM inference tasks.
